tagline: A 120 nm resort coast with brutal road transfers — and the sea running flat and direct alongside it.
summary: Jamaica's tourism economy lines up along the north coast: Montego Bay (Sangster International and the all-inclusive belt), Falmouth's purpose-built cruise pier, Ocho Rios, and the quiet luxury of Port Antonio — with Negril on the western tip. The island set a record ~2.96 million stopover arrivals in 2023/24, yet almost every guest moves between airport, ship and resort on long, winding coastal roads: Montego Bay to Ocho Rios is 1.5–2 hours by car but ~47 nm of sheltered water. A foiling shuttle network maps directly onto the airport-transfer, cruise-excursion and resort-hopping demand already paying for slow road journeys.

demand_signals.label: Record stopover arrivals
demand_signals.value: ~2.96M stopover arrivals (2023/24, record) · ~4.3M total visitors incl. cruise (2024)
demand_signals.note: Tourism is concentrated on exactly the coast a water network would serve

demand_signals.label: Sangster International throughput
demand_signals.note: The island's main tourism gateway sits on Montego Bay's shoreline — nearly every arriving guest faces a 1–2 hr road transfer east or west

demand_signals.label: Three north-coast cruise ports
demand_signals.value: Montego Bay, Falmouth (Oasis-class pier) and Ocho Rios
demand_signals.note: Falmouth was purpose-built for the world's largest cruise ships; shore-excursion movement between the three ports is all by road today

demand_signals.label: Road-vs-water gap
demand_signals.value: MoBay→Ocho Rios ~1.5–2 hrs by road vs ~47 nm of sheltered water
demand_signals.note: The coastal highway winds through towns; the sea route is the straight line — same for Negril (~40 nm) and Falmouth (~18 nm)

demand_signals.label: Established on-water excursion market
demand_signals.value: Catamaran party/snorkel fleets operate daily from MoBay, Ocho Rios & Negril
demand_signals.note: Island Routes and independent operators prove guests already pay to be on this water — transfers are the unserved layer

use_cases.title: Airport-to-resort water transfers
use_cases.body: Sangster International sits on the bay: meet arrivals at a Montego Bay jetty and deliver guests to Round Hill, Half Moon, Falmouth or Ocho Rios resorts by water — turning the worst part of a Jamaica holiday into its first highlight.

use_cases.title: Cruise-port excursion shuttles
use_cases.body: Falmouth ↔ Montego Bay (~18 nm) and Falmouth ↔ Ocho Rios day-loops give cruise lines a premium, zero-emission shore-excursion product between the island's three piers, Doctor's Cave Beach and Dunn's River Falls.

use_cases.title: Quiet-luxury east: Port Antonio
use_cases.body: Errol Flynn Marina — the island's premier full-service marina — anchors a low-volume, high-value foiling link from Ocho Rios (~40 nm) to the Blue Lagoon coast, keeping the east end quiet precisely because the road is long.

use_cases.title: Kingston harbour & the capital corridor
use_cases.body: Kingston's huge natural harbour already has a Port Royal ferry heritage; a north-coast ↔ Kingston hybrid link (~130 nm) connects the resort economy to the business capital without the trans-island mountain road.

journeys.today: 1.5–2 hours in a transfer van on the winding A1/A3 coastal road — the standard, dreaded start to an Ocho Rios holiday.
journeys.with_navier: A ~47 nm flight along the reef-sheltered north coast, flat and quiet past Falmouth and Discovery Bay, arriving at the resort jetty rested instead of carsick.

journeys.today: Shore-excursion buses queue out of the port gate and crawl the 35–45 minute road into MoBay's traffic.
journeys.with_navier: An ~18 nm foiling hop straight off the pier to the Hip Strip's beach jetties — more beach time, zero bus.

journeys.today: About 1.5 hours by road around the island's western parishes.
journeys.with_navier: A ~40 nm run around the northwest coast past Lucea, landing on Bloody Bay's calm water at the top of Seven Mile Beach.

journeys.today: A slow 2+ hour drive deters most visitors — which keeps the east empty but also starves it.
journeys.with_navier: A ~40 nm hop past Oracabessa and Noël Coward's Blue Harbour to the island's best marina — quiet luxury reached quietly.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire north-coast resort corridor is Pioneer II territory: MoBay↔Falmouth ~18 nm, MoBay↔Negril ~40 nm, MoBay↔Ocho Rios ~47 nm and Ocho Rios↔Port Antonio ~40 nm — all comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, on water sheltered by the island's fringing reef.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (700 nm hybrid) adds the capital link — north coast ↔ Kingston (~130 nm around either end of the island) — and regional reach such as Montego Bay ↔ Grand Cayman (~270 nm), with no charging infrastructure needed at the far end.

competitive_landscape: Jamaica's water is busy with excursion product — catamaran party cruises, snorkel trips and Island Routes' branded adventures out of MoBay, Ocho Rios and Negril — and Kingston runs a small Port Royal ferry heritage. That is daily, paid, on-water demand. But point-to-point movement is owned by road: JUTA/Knutsford transfer vans and tour buses carry virtually every guest between airport, pier and resort. No scheduled coastal passenger service exists on the north coast; the transfer layer is wide open.

precedents.what: ~$100M, ~100-vessel electric foiling network with JIH Global, 3-year phased rollout, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: The template for a resort-nation transfer network — phased, resort-anchored, and built around airport-to-resort water arrivals exactly like Sangster's geography.

seasonality: Year-round season; peak tourism Dec–Apr coincides with the steadiest trade-wind weather. The north coast is largely protected by fringing reef, with afternoon trade-wind chop that foiling rides above. Hurricane season (Jun–Nov, statistically peaking Aug–Oct) requires flexible scheduling and safe-harbour plans — Montego Bay, Falmouth and Kingston's enclosed harbour all provide haul-out and shelter options.
regulatory_note: Ports and piers are governed by the Port Authority of Jamaica; vessel certification and crewing fall under the Maritime Authority of Jamaica. The Tourism Enhancement Fund and Jamaica Tourist Board actively fund visitor-experience and transfer-modernisation projects, and Jamaica's national energy transition plan favours electrified transport — a clean, quiet coastal fleet aligns with both the tourism and energy agendas.
